newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures ends up on LME gains.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures ends up on LME gains.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended slightly up on Monday due to gains on the London Metal Exchange last Friday, traders said.
The most active August 1998 contract ended at 22,970 yuan ($2,769) per tonne, rising 120 yuan. It opened at an intra-day high of 23,040 and hit a low of 22,930.
May rose 50 to 23,100, June 50 to 23,030, July 100 to 22,970 and September 80 to 22,940.
Combined volume rose to 19,250 tonnes from 14,330.
Copper opened high but profit-taking then pushed prices steadily down for most of the session.
Traders said the LME gains boosted the confidence of Shanghai's long position holders but thin volume indicated many investors were sticking to the sidelines.
"The LME gains were the major factor today but most investors seemed to be buying for quick profit," a trader said. "They are taking a wary attitude due to a lack of major market-moving news."
Traders said spot copper supported futures prices.
Physical copper prices are around 23,200 yuan per tonne in the Shanghai area.
Traders said the LME would continue to be an important factor affecting prices of Shanghai copper futures in the next few days due to a lack of domestic market-moving news.
"If there is no fresh market-moving news, copper is likely to move around the 23,000 yuan level in the next few days," a second trader said.
Aluminium ended down. May fell 230 to 15,140 and June 210 to 15,290. Combined volume rose to 2,080 tonnes from 1,290.
